parakeet: Some people don't want a dialogue. They want a dopamine hit of dominance. But I wasn't called to spar with superstition. I'm here to build with the willing. Debate should never be a reward for ignorance. And it should never be a stage for someone who's already shown up with a closed mind and a loaded question. So if you're wondering why I want to engage your favorite apologist, preacher, or pew-sitting provocateur, it's simple. I don't debate those who mistake authority for accuracy and confuse confidence with competence. As Dr. Clark reminded us, I only debate my equals. All others, I teach. And sometimes I just move on because class is dismissed. And as a special bonus, I wanted to give you this one. Religious gods don't exist outside the books that claim them. Let's stop pretending that gods are free-floating truths just waiting to be discovered. Religious gods don't exist independently. They exist textually, they exist mythologically, they exist within the confines of the stories, the books, and the claims that birth them. And once you examine the book and the claims, the whole house of worship collapses like a stage prop. Let me make it plain. I didn't lose faith because of pain, hurt, or disappointment. I stopped believing because the foundation itself was false. The entire structure of belief was built on two flawed assumptions. Number one, that the Bible was indeed true. And number two, that the people who passed it down had verified that truth.
